sections.content: How many people stayed in Cheltenham after gaining qualifications?

Cheltenham is a large town in the South West. Cheltenham also has a university.

Cheltenham has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Cheltenham ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 4,160 state-school pupils from Cheltenham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,625 (39%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,160 (28%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Cheltenham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Cheltenham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Cheltenham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Cheltenham move to?

Of Cheltenham's graduates, 650 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 65 of those graduates (10%) were living fairly locally, in the Cheltenham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Cheltenham's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 280 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those qualified non-graduates (18%) were living fairly locally, in the Cheltenham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Cheltenham's GCSE cohort:

  • 425 graduates left the South West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 105 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South West
  • the most common region they moved to was the West Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 55% of graduates and 37% of qualified non-graduates living in Cheltenham had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 2,095 graduates and 1,355 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Cheltenham. This is compared with the 1,625 graduates and 1,160 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 45% of the graduates had also lived in Cheltenham as GCSE pupils, while 55% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Cheltenham in 2018 to 2019, 63% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 37% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
